sections.markdown: Black Knights** are enemies in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Black Knights are an order of knights who are devoted servants of Messmer the Impaler, serving as the primary force in his army. Having absolute loyalty to their master, the Black Knights possess an iron conviction to their Crusade, and they never yield nor doubt their purpose, being strongly dedicated to purging the Realm of Shadow,

Wearing black armor ornamentally and etched in gold, they carry weapons and shields of black steel, decorated with golden embellishments, and are imbued with Erdtree incantations. The Black Knights also seem to emit a rotten odor from their gauntlets and greaves. The cause may be from the tainted nature of the blood that stains their armor, or it may stem from their blackened souls, which fester as a result of endless slaughter.

Despite their devoted loyalty, however, not all Black Knights serve Messmer without doubt; both Black Knight Commander Andreas and his son and second-in-command Black Knight Captain Huw rebelled against Messmer upon learning of his serpentine nature. For their betrayal, they were ultimately imprisoned in underground tombs.

Bestial incantations**, also known as **beast incantations**, are a type of Incantation in Elden Ring. They are used primarily by Gurranq, Beast Clergyman and the Vulgar Militia. These incantations harness the primal power of beasts, focusing on robustness, healing, and delivering devastating physical attacks. The Clawmark Seal and Cinquedea both increase the effectiveness of offensive bestial incantations.

They all have a very low Faith requirement.

- Clawmark Seal increases Attack Power by 10% when held in an active hand, and by 21% when wielded in each hand (stacks with Cinquedea).

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Blackflame**, also known as , is a type of flame in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Blackflame was weighty, alluring fire conjured by Godslayer incantations. Drawn from faith and the power of the Rune of Death, its black-and-white flames could burn away the very gods in ancient times.

Following the War Against the Giants, the beguiling blackflame enthralled Amon and other Fire Monks loyal to the Giants' Flame. Those who fled their duties formed the Blackflame Monks, aligning themselves with the Empyrean Gloam-Eyed Queen and her Godskin Apostles. Together, they launched a violent god hunt, during which the black flame was their armor within. However, Queen Marika commanded her Shadowbound Beast and half-brother, Maliketh, to defeat the Gloam-Eyed Queen and her Apostles. She removed the Rune of Death from the Elden Ring, and Maliketh sealed it in his black blade. The Golden Order was born, and the true power of the black flame was lost.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Battle of Aeonia** was an event that occurred during the Shattering in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The Battle of Aeonia was the infamous final act of the Shattering, which decimated the central region of Caelid, now known as the Swamp of Aeonia. The conflict arose when Malenia the Severed confronted General Radahn regarding Miquella's vow. Malenia and her undefeated Cleanrot Knight army marched southward through Liurnia of the Lakes and Limgrave to reach Caelid, where they met Radahn's Redmane forces in battle.

The Demigods were evenly matched, fighting to a standstill in a field southwest of Sellia, Town of Sorcery. The stalemate ended when Malenia, in an attempt to kill Radahn, snapped her Unalloyed Gold Needle by stabbing herself, whispering in her rival's ear: *"Miquella awaits thee, O promised consort."* This act triggered her very first rotflower bloom, unleashing the baleful scarlet rot she had fought her whole life to contain. Although the Empyrean gained tremendous strength, Malenia was unable to kill Radahn and quickly succumbed to a deep, coma-like slumber.

sections.heading: Aftermath
sections.markdown:
Malenia and Radahn's duel ended in a stalemate. Her Scarlet Aeonia scattered Aeonian butterflies and terraformed the landscape, driving back the Redmane Knights, but their leader survived. Radahn's Great Rune burned to resist the scarlet rot, though his mind was quickly consumed, reducing him to no more than a wandering, feral beast. In defeat, the Redmanes likewise burned the Red Lion crest on their left breasts to indicate their resolve, vowing to remain behind to act as a smoldering bulwark against the encroaching scarlet rot. Miquella of the Haligtree rescued Redmane Freyja from the Swamp of Aeonia, cured her rotting sickness, and charmed her into his service.

The festering Swamp spawned pests and other Servants of Rot, though Malenia would not embrace them. She lingered for a time before Cleanrot Knight Finlay pulled her from the bog and carried her back to the Haligtree. However, Malenia's daughters later emerged from the swamp, each child taken in by Sage Gowry. Romina, Saint of the Bud reached out to the abandoned scarlet butterflies and drew some of them to the Realm of Shadow.

Ultimately, none of the Demigods succeeded in becoming Elden Lord or the God of a new era, and they were abandoned by the Greater Will. Some time later, the guidance of Grace was extended to the Tarnished, who were called back to the Lands Between to claim the Great Runes, become Elden Lord, and restore the Golden Order.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Assault on Volcano Manor** was an event that occurred during The Shattering in Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
A gluttonous serpent dwelled on Mt. Gelmir in ancient times, feeding on human sacrifices provided by its followers. Although the Serpent-God was slain long ago, Praetor Rykard, a Demigod, later rediscovered the ancient hexes of the mountain. Despite being a ruthless justiciar, who mercilessly prosecuted—and tortured—those accused of heresy and other crimes, he grew disillusioned with the Golden Order.

In the wake of the Shattering, Rykard and his siblings each claimed shards of the great Elden Ring. Discontent with struggling over Queen Marika's scraps of power, he viewed the abasing war with total contempt. Believing that the gods were no different, Rykard turned to taking by force, launching a blasphemous insurgency against the Erdtree and the Greater Will. Many knights believed his ambitions are noble and made him worthy of sovereignty, pledging their support to his cause.

sections.heading: Assault
sections.markdown:
A war with no glory, the Assault on Volcano Manor is said to have been the most appalling battle in the Shattering. The conflict took place on Mt. Gelmir, between Rykard's army and the forces of Leyndell. The squalid, the sick, and the blasphemous are said to have participated in the battle, which went on without end. The attackers brought the Jar Cannon to the assault, however it was discovered that nobody knew how to use it.

Rykard would eventually feed himself, great rune and all, to the great serpent, known as the God-Devouring Serpent, an ancient traitor of the Erdtree, and he became one with the serpent. With his own lofty ambition turning into gluttonous depravity, Rykard began devouring on his own champions, feeding them to the bowels of the God-Devouring Serpent. The devoured champions would then become part of Rykard's "family" so they can devour the gods together. Disturbed by what their lord had become and the battles waged in his name being costly, Rykard's own men deserted him, no longer able to abide the consequences of his blasphemy. Those who remained came to be known as Recusants.

Psychologically affected by their experience in the assault, most of the soldiers in Leyndell's army eventually became afflicted by Frenzy - leaving them in a state of madness - and seemingly resorted to cannibalism, consuming the bodies of the dead, which became a sickening reality across the battlefields.

The blood star is an occult entity whose power is channeled by Faith-based Thorn Sorceries. It exists beyond the Lands Between and may only be glimpsed by those deprived of light. It is deeply tied to Blood Loss and the Briars of Sin.

The Guilty Sorcerers and other exiled criminals beheld the blood star after their eyes were gouged out during the War Against the Giants. Soon after, they began issuing blood sacrifices to weave bloodthorn spirals with aberrant sorceries.

Despite its cosmic origin, sorcerous practices involving the blood star were prohibited by the Academy of Raya Lucaria. Heretics who pursued it, such Mad Tongue Alberich, produced a special red glintstone saturated with blood. Such a power is comparable to that of Death hexes.

sections.markdown: Knight Bernahl's nameless Finger Maiden threw herself into the Forge of the Giants. According to unused concept she had detailed appearance and failed to become a kindling maiden. In full release, she only be mentioned in Beast Champion Set’s description and her ritual is presumed successful, considering that Bernahl's golden summon sign in the Crumbling Farum Azula requires no prerequisites.

sections.heading: Location
sections.markdown: - Her presumed charred remains kneel in Dejection at the Shack of the Lofty on the Mountaintops of the Giants. Looting them grants the Traveling Maiden Hood, Traveling Maiden Robe, Traveling Maiden Gloves, and Traveling Maiden Boots. This finger maiden is also suspected of being Juno Hoslow, Knight of Blood‘s maiden.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- An NPC version of Bernahl's Finger Maiden was planned for the Smoldering Church in Caelid, but was ultimately scrapped prior to the and may no longer be canonical.
 - Only her face data, equipped armor, initial location, and Japanese dialogue subtitles made it into the game; information about this version of her character is based on an unofficial translation of the Japanese script and may contain inaccuracies. An official English source text has yet to emerge or does not exist.
 - She wore the Bloodsoaked Mask, Finger Maiden Robe (Altered), Traveling Maiden Gloves, and Traveling Maiden Boots. She was bald with golden eyes and burns covering her face.
 - She asked to be burned with various flames to become a Kindling Maiden, but was ultimately unfit. The Giants' Flame would not find purchase within her in the way it does Melina, whose story she paralleled.
 - This NPC was replaced with Anastasia, Tarnished-Eater, a false Finger Maiden who invades at the Smoldering Church. Anastasia also invades near the Volcano Manor, which was where Bernahl went after his maiden perished.
 - Bernahl's Finger Maiden described the Fire Monks as giant.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Asimi, Silver Tear**, later known as **Asimi, Eternal King**, was a Silver Tear character that was cut from Elden Ring. They asked to enter the player's body to aid them on their quest. Information about them is limited and may no longer be canonical.

sections.heading: Location
sections.markdown: Asimi was located at the Artist's Shack in Limgrave.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: Asimi was a silver tear that gained sentience and the ability to speak, living in fear of death. An arcane creature of mimicry, they came from a mother chalice in the Eternal City—the cradle of their kind—with dreams of one day becoming Sovereign Eternal.

sections.heading: Asimi's Quest
sections.markdown:
Asimi would have identified the Tarnished as the one fated to become Elden Lord, offering power in exchange for protection. Should the player accept, Asimi was inhaled through a kiss, living inside their new host.

Upon hearing the great underground rivers of their home, Asimi would have urged the player to visit the Eternal Cities, where special chalices could be found. Asimi wished to quench their thirst by drinking from these cradle chalices to become a more perfect whole. After collecting the tears from each chalice, Asimi likely exited the Tarnished to follow their footsteps.

Asimi likely morphed into the Tarnished and attacked them, much like the Mimic Tear and Stray Mimic Tear bosses.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- A unique "kissing" animation would have triggered when the player accepted Asimi inside.
- Melina offered unique dialogue if Asimi was present inside the Tarnished.
- They likely dropped or granted the Mimic Tear Ashes.
- The mother chalice was the most sacred to Asimi, and the cradle of their kind. It was suffused with the blessings of the stars.
- Radagon of the Golden Order also sought to become a perfect whole and reign for eternity.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Astrologers** were a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
At some point long before the rise of the Erdtree, the ancient astrologers established themselves in the Mountaintops of the Giants, the highest peaks of the Lands Between, where they dwelled at the Stargazer's Ruins and read fate in the stars. They considered the Fire Giants their allies and lived in peace alongside them.

One astrologer glimpsed the Primeval Current, and the stars showered the Lands Between with their amber: Glintstone, a crystalline substance bearing the vitality of the stars. This revelation gave rise to the first glintstone sorcery, the legendary Founding Rain of Stars. From then on, astrologers embedded glintstone at the tips of their staves, using them as catalysts for sorcery. In doing so, they became the precursor to the modern Glintstone Sorcerers, who continued their traditions. Some among them even fashioned Primal Glintstone Blades, slicing open their own hearts to bind their souls to primal glintstones before death.

Among the astrologers was Rennala, who spent her youth gazing at the night sky and following the stars. One day she beheld the Full Moon upon the Mountaintops, and from that moment she was set upon her path. Rennala later enchanted the Academy of Raya Lucaria with her moon magic and rose as a champion. There she became master of the academy and queen of Liurnia of the Lakes, establishing House Caria as royalty.

The Carians continued the astrologers’ legacy, constructing immense telescopes to chart the heavens. Yet with the coming of the Age of the Erdtree, the Golden Order supplanted the fate once governed by the stars, and Carian astrology fell into decline. Even so, the Carians preserved their heritage: Caria Manor safeguarded the Sword of Night and Flame as a relic of their ancient alliance with the Fire Giants, their preceptors wore wide hats inscribed with the motions of the stars, and the Stargazer Heirloom, commemorating Rennala’s legend, passed into the keeping of her daughter, Ranni the Witch.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Bearded Ancient Dynasty Statues***, unofficially referred to as *Elden John*, *Fellden John*, *Ancient Dynast*, *Ancient Dynasty God*, *Bearded Elder*, *Uhl King*, *Uld King*, and other names in the community, are objects in Elden Ring. All information about the statues and unseen character they depict is conjectural, based on visual details and contextual clues.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown: The old statues portray a bald-headed elder with a long, braided beard and a missing right eye, dressed in a hooded robe and holding a stone tablet to his chest with elongated arms, though individual examples vary. Those on stone-coffin ships show him in his most human form, flanked by maiden-and-lord pairings, and may be among the earliest. Works attributed to the Ancient Dynasty give him a damaged right eye and arboreal traits—most notably a root-like beard—and depict him embracing one half of a broken tablet with tightly crossed arms, the discarded half placed at his feet; the held fragment bears a tree, while the other contains a ringed world map or sun. Statues at the Cocoon of the Empyrean omit the rejected tablet and replace his legs with roots. The figures at The Four Belfries, likely the most recent, emphasize his emergence from dense roots or dead branches. His robes have extended sleeves, and he raises his hands to his chest. His legs and both tablets are absent.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
A bearded man was revered in the Ancient Dynasty that existed long before the age of the Erdtree. His heroic followers were sent off with Great Grave Glovewort in great stone coffin ships for burial at sea, drifting towards the Lands Between. When the massive arks finally washed up on the Cerulean Coast, their contents had putrified into a viscous sludge of bruise-colored putrescence. Though tainted and impure, the Deathbirds nonetheless cleansed the putrid remains in their ghostflame kilns, until they one day stopped.

His followers established a series of palaces along the Siofra and Ainsel Rivers, where claymen priests used crude weapons made from shards of fallen meteorites, which also arrived from outside the realm. They constructed the Hallowhorn Grounds, Uhl Palace Ruins, Uld Palace Ruins, Lake of Rot, Grand Cloister, and Mohgwyn Palace, and later The Four Belfries. At some point, their ancient dynasty collapsed, and the tablet-clutching god's name was forgotten.

The Ancestral Followers later worshipped Ancestor Spirits among the dynastic ruins. Their ritual implements evoked the power of horns, trees, and Deathbirds. The followers' faith existed beyond the influence of the Erdtree, asserting that new life arises from death, and from Death, one gains power.

After the outer god of Rot was sealed away in the Grand Cloister, the Kindred of Rot prayed toward scarlet rot-infested statues of the bearded man.

The Mohgwyn Dynasty worshipped a large statue of the bearded man at the Mohgwyn Dynasty Mausoleum, which faced the Cocoon of the Empyrean, where eight smoldering statues of the bearded man portray him without legs, rising upward.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Some Ancient Dynasty stelae depict him tending tall trees.
- Rugs and folding screens in Leyndell, Royal Capital depict clones of the bearded elder growing like fruit on a tree, suggesting a link between the Ancient Dynasty and the Golden Lineage. It also indicates that the statues may not all depict the same individual.
- He may be related to the Suppressing Pillar because of its similarity to ancient dynasty architecture.
- His context connects him to various outer gods, including Death, Night, the Fell God of Fire, the Formless Mother, and even the Greater Will.
 - He has only one eye, but plenty of facial hair, similar to the Fell God.
 - His likeness seemingly appears with and without the hood on the Winged Scythe, linking him to Ancient Death. This weapon symbolizes white-winged maidens, who are said to be Death's gentle envoys.
 - The Putrescent Knight's head seems to contain starlight.
 - Mohg, whose Omen blood was aflame by the Formless Mother, seeks to establish a Mohgwyn Dynasty within the Ancient Dynastic ruins.
 - After the crusade ravaged the hornsent, they found the Formless Mother in the shadow of their ancestor, and transformed into Bloodfiends. Some sought out eternal rest from St. Trina in the Stone Coffin Fissure.
 - He may be related to Metyr, Mother of Fingers, who once communed with the Greater Will through her bubble-like microcosm, as Claymen Sorceries produce Magic bubbles within which oracles were once found, and Oracle Envoys use holy bubbles to herald the arrival of a new god. Maris, Fathom of Night, also known as the Augur and "master of bubbles," is another likely candidate.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- The discarded tablet texture is sourced from the (also known as the *Imago Mundi* or *Mappa mundi*)—the earliest known world map—which depicts ancient , often dubbed the “cradle of civilization,” as a sun or star-shaped region with two major rivers.
- Both tablets display a tree on one face, and a map on the other, but their reverse sides are not visible in regular play; they most likely share textures for performance and storage efficiency.
- The Bearded Elder shares many traits with , the All-Father from . Most notably are his association with trees, missing right eye, and role as a .
- The figure and his paired tablets also allude to , who received two inscribed by the . His appearance on stone coffins also likens him to because "Noah's Ark" are their filenames.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Champion** was one of the five playable characters . Unlike the Prophet and Warrior origins, Champion, along with Bloody Wolf and Enchanted Knight, would not appear in the final game, though its armor and weapon would be inherited by the Hero origin and the shield would end up being carried by the Samurai origin.

sections.heading: Recreating
sections.markdown:
Though the class isn't fully available as a starting Origin, even with the Hero carrying a majority of its equipment, it can be recreated.

The weapon and the shield, Battle Axe and Red Thorn Roundshield, can be gained by either starting as a Hero (this is also the only way to have 2 of them) or buying it from the Twin Maiden Husks and by starting as a Samurai or buying it from the Nomadic Merchant at Castle Morne Rampart in Weeping Peninsula, for the axe and shield respectively.

The Armor Set is more out of the way if not gained by starting as the Hero origin, as it's bought from the Nomadic Merchant in southern Caelid, southwest of the Southern Aeonia Swamp Bank Site of Grace and on the road split leading towards Redmane Castle.

The Finger Seal is bought from the Twin Maiden Husks or by starting as either either the Prophet or the Confessor origin, while Dragonfire requires a Dragon Heart (most easily gained by defeating Flying Dragon Agheel) and then sacrificing it at either the Church of Dragon Communion found past Coastal Cave in Limgrave or at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in southern Caelid.

sections.heading: Suitable Origins
sections.markdown:
The Hero origin is obviously a good start if trying to recreate this class, seeing as it wears the correct Armor Set and both has a Battle Axe and is the only way to get two of them without starting another Journey. It will need 7 points in Faith and 1 in Arcane to cast Dragonfire but will probably be better off by switching the Finger Seal for a Clawmark Seal to better synergize with the Strength/Faith build it's more naturally set up for.

The Prophet origin could also be a decent base since it can wield the Battle Axe one-handed with only 1 more point in Strength and cast Dragonfire with 1 more point in Arcane, but will lack any fitting equipment to start with.

sections.heading: Build Optimization
sections.markdown: For people who wish to select an origin that will have the most optimal stat distribution for a build with the fewest stat points wasted, Confessor is objectively the worst choice. Origins become more efficient when they have lower stats as this means the low stat can be ignored and the points can instead be invested in attributes that the build makes use of. With Confessor's lowest stat values being a 9 in Intelligence and a 9 in Arcane, the origin only has a maximum of 2 points it can potentially save when compared with Wretch. Even in a build where none of its other points are wasted, Prophet, Hero and Vagabond save more stat points overall than Confessor, as their lowest stats are all at 7 which grants them far more build potential. Note that these builds are not necessarily "good", they are just what this origin is better at than any other.

sections.heading: Sword of Night and Flame
sections.markdown: Despite the issues inherent to confessor it has one single solitary niche, being one of the two most optimal origins to build for the Sword of Night and Flame. It shares this tie with Astrologer and both origins save 1 stat point on this build when compared to Wretch. The only notable difference between the two options is that Confessor has 2 less Mind than Astrologer. This gap in FP does not affect the number of times you are able to use the sword's weapon skill, meaning that Confessor is overall the most optimal origin if you specifically do not want to cast spells as part of this build, or invest in being able to cast the weapon skill more often.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Catch Flame** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Flame incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
- Sold for 600 Runes by Brother Corhyn.
- Should Corhyn die before purchasing this incantation, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them Corhyn's Bell Bearing.
- Starting equipment for the Prophet Origin.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown: Conjure a small burst of flames from the hand, that has Fire Attack Power equal to 225% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 10 FP per cast.
- Costs 17 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot.
- Deals 7 Stance damage.
- Can be chain-cast continuously, provided the player has sufficient amounts of FP.
- Casting this incantation directly after a roll, jump, or backstep makes the casting time slightly shorter, making it much more dynamic than many other, slower spells.
- Moves the caster slightly forward with each use.
- Despite using the Giants' Flame, this spell does not generate a spell sigil when cast, making it ineligible for a boost from the Giant's Seal.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.markdown:
- With its rapid casting time, Catch Flame excels as a quick, close-range option for dispatching enemies. However, its small area of effect and short range make it less reliable against agile or fast-moving targets.
- A potent damage-dealing spell throughout the game thanks to its more than decent damage and extremely quick casting time, and available on a lot of Incantations build with only a minimal amount of Faith.
 - It is especially potent as an early-game tool for players who can manage the low FP cost compared to their meager FP pool.
 - Highly efficient as a melee spell for pure Faith builds.
- Casting Catch Flame immediately before Magma Breath significantly reduces the cast time of the latter, enabling quicker execution in combat.
 - When chained into Magma Breath mid-air, Catch Flame modifies the casting animation into a faster, more fluid spray, allowing players to seamlessly chain another Magma Breath cast.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Like Fire's Deadly Sin and Flame Sling, this incantation does not produce a spell sigil when cast, indicating that it technically doesn't belong to the Giants' Flame subtype and isn't boosted by the Giant's Seal.
Brother Corhyn was one of the prophets exiled for glimpsing the forbidden flame of ruin, a transgression that led to banishment. 
- Catch Flame closely resembles the Combustion spell from the *Dark Souls* series.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Broadsword** is a straight sword found in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
- Starting equipment for the Confessor class.
- Nomadic Merchant southeast of Coastal Cave, beneath the collapsed structure.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The default skill is useful for breaking the guard of blocking enemies with the light attack version or for breaking their Stance with the heavy attack version.
- Always has the highest Attack Power (AP) of all regular Straight Swords, with the exception of the Quality Affinity, primarily due to its high base damage being able to compensate for its somewhat mediocre scaling.
 - Since it's acquirable extremely early, as soon as the tutorial is completed, this weapon is a useful tool for potentially the entire game.
- Surprisingly, compared to its predecessors from previous game, this weapon isn't short but merely of average length.
- Leans towards Strength for Cold and Blood/Poison affinities.
- Despite having the highest damage and scaling on its Heavy affinity it actually gives slightly weaker Strength-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Heavy, Quality, or Fire affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Ground Slam, Storm Blade, and Flame of the Redmanes (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Heavy).
- Has a unique heavy attack and rolling attack, shared with the Cane Sword, replacing the usual thrusts with a broad, sweeping strike and an upward cut specifically.
 - This is mostly a disadvantage. While the unique heavy attack is mostly good, it lacks the Pierce damage of the usual Straight Sword heavy attack and thus can't counter-hit attacking foes, while the unique rolling attack is very lacking in reach.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.markdown:
- Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
- Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- All non-physical Affinities lower all types of guarded damage negation by 5%, except for the associated element where the damage negation increases by 25% and another element also increases by 15%.
 - Magic negation receives the secondary 15% negation bonus on Sacred and Cold affinities, Fire negation gets the increase on Lightning affinity, Lightning negation gets the increase on Fire and Flame Art affinities, and Holy negation gets the increase on Magic affinity.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Carian Knight's Sword** is a straight sword found in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown: Held by a Carriage located in the northwest region of Liurnia of the Lakes, between the Northern Liurnia Lake Shore and The Four Belfries Sites of Grace.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The locked, innate skill, Carian Grandeur, while not unique and reliant on its weaker Intelligence-scaling, is still very strong if it can hit. Best used as a replacement for a Critical Attack or while lying in ambush since it charges somewhat slowly.
- Gains the most Attack Power (AP) from a hybrid Strength/Intelligence build (616 AP from having 45 Strength, 10 Dexterity, and 45 Intelligence), a bit less from a pure Strength build (609 AP from 80 Strength, 10 Dexterity, and 18 Intelligence), and far less from a pure Intelligence build (576 AP from 10 Strength, 10 Dexterity, and 80 Intelligence).
 - Note that since the skill's damage is entirely reliant on the character's Intelligence and the weapon's Intelligence-scaling, the skill will be weaker on the pure Strength build compared to the other two builds.
 - Since the Carian Knight's Sword innate Intelligence-scaling is fairly poor, strengthening the skill and the sword's Attack Power together is somewhat difficult, with only the ease of upgrading weapons with Somber Smithing Stones over those needing Smithing Stones keeping it in front of regular Magic affinity weapons with this skill equipped.
- Has a unique blocking heavy attack, shared with the Lazuli Glintstone Sword. While this can make attacking into an attacking foe a bit less punishing, the resulting Stamina damage that will be taken if hit can prevent the user from attacking or rolling away.
 - While the brief hit-stun taken by shields isn't suffered when hit, the low Stability means that using the unique heavy attack is highly likely to result in a stun from being guardbroken.
 - Stability can be increased by 10% via two-handing and then further by the Greatshield Talisman.
 - While the uncharged unique heavy attack deals the same amount of Stance damage as a normal uncharged heavy attack, the charged version only deals 1.5 times more Stance damage instead of the regular straight sword charged version which deals 3 times more Stance damage.

sections.markdown: Commander Niall** is an optional boss in Elden Ring. Defeating him will unlock the Commander Niall achievement.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: Commander Niall, a veteran general of Castle Sol, offered his prosthesis in exchange for the lives of imprisoned knights, forming an army of no nation. A lone survivor, Niall commands the spirits of deceased knights to defend his master, who has long passed. Niall guards a chest containing the Haligtree Secret Medallion (Left), one-half of the Medallion required to gain access to the Consecrated Snowfield, the land of Miquella's Haligtree.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.markdown: At the beginning of the fight, Niall summons the spirits of two Banished Knights, one with a sword and shield, and the other wielding dual swords. Niall will be relatively passive while the knights are alive, instead buffing them until they have both been defeated or his health has been reduced to half. Both Banished Knights will inflict Frostbite with their attacks. Niall himself uses a mixture of lightning and frost-based attacks. He can imbue his prosthesis with lightning and perform kicks and stomps, and he can use his halberd to generate frost.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Borealis the Freezing Fog** is an optional Great Enemy boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Borealis the Freezing Fog was one of the ice dragons, who were lords of the Mountaintops before the Fire Giants chased them from the peak.

The dragon Borealis patrols the frozen expanse of the Freezing Lake in the northeastern Mountaintops of the Giants. He emerges from a thick white fog, which he exhales clouds that inflict Frostbite.

sections.heading: Location
sections.markdown: Borealis the Freezing Fog is located in the Mountaintops of the Giants, patrolling the frozen lake southeast of the Freezing Lake Site of Grace. The nearest Grace is Spiritcaller Cave.

sections.heading: Drops
sections.markdown: - Defeating Borealis the Freezing Fog will award one Dragon Heart, 100,000 Runes, and will unlock Borealis's Mist, which can be obtained at the altar in the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for two Dragon Hearts.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.markdown:
Instead of flames, Borealis exhales Dragonice and Borealis's Mist.
- Borealis inflicts Frostbite with his breath attacks and roars. His attacks include:
 - Frost Breath: Borealis exhales a cone of freezing fog, which lingers and applies Frostbite.
 - Frost Stomp: Stomps on the ground, creating a shockwave of ice that deals AoE damage and builds Frostbite.
 - Frost Wing Sweep: Swings his massive wings, releasing icy projectiles that track players in the area.
 - Roar: Releases a deafening roar that briefly staggers players and applies frost buildup.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Borealis the Freezing Fog counts as a Dragon-type enemy and is vulnerable to anti-dragon effects.
- Furled Fingers and Spirit Ashes are allowed in this encounter.
- Defeating Borealis the Freezing Fog will unlock Borealis's Mist, which can be obtained at the altar in the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for two Dragon Hearts.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown: - Borealis is the only ice dragon in the game.
